NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for
  viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday following the
  meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 865 014 450, Meeting Password: 650005. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak
  using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  ZOOM app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App
  Store), by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 865 014 450, Meeting Password: 650005
  Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using  the
  following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand"
  option at the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which
  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 14, 2020

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:10 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DMV/DONATE LIFE MONTH

  MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring April as Donate Life Month.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DAY OF REMEMBRANCE OF THE ARMENIAN GENOCIDE

  MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring April 24, 2020 as a day of
  remembrance of the Armenian Genocide of 1915-1923. COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN shared how his family was affected by the Armenian Genocide and
  expressed the importance of continuing to bring attention to crimes against humanity
  so that they do not continue to occur.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested that items 5E and 5F (Equestrian
  Committee Minutes of February 24, 2020 and the 2019 Housing Element Annual
  Progress Report) be removed for individual consideration.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-D APPROVED AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 14, 2020
 B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 10, 2020

  APPROVED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 10, 2020

  APPROVED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MARCH 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62643 THROUGH 62704 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $336,775.29 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040120 THROUGH
  040320 IN THE AMOUNT OF $103,195.60 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $439,970.89 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 24, 2020

  Recommendation: Receive and File.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride scheduled
  for May 9, 2020 as discussed in the Equestrian Committee meeting minutes. City
  Manager Grammer explained that this event would be postponed, and will be
  discussed at the April 20, 2020 Park & Activities Commission meeting.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL requested the following typos be corrected in the
  final minutes: round pin corrected to round pen, and Pam Shacter corrected to
  Schachter.

F.  2019 HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT

  Recommendation: Receive and File.

  Planning Manager Naughton explained that the report was prepared by staff in
  response to a question by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the level of detail provided within the
  report, including addresses of properties. Planning Manager Naughton explained
  that the details provided were requirements.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN clarified that the different totals reported on
  different pages of the report vary based on the dates of the occurrences.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 5E and 5F.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 14, 2020
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEMS FROM MEETING OF
  MARCH 3, 2020 - CRENSHAW BOULEVARD AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH AND AT CHADWICK LANE - CONCERNS OF ACADEMY HILLS HOMES
  ASSOCIATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the two Traffic and Safety
  Committee items: 1) Crenshaw Boulevard/Palos Verdes Drive North - Install two
  signs that state: “Right Hand Turn on Red Must Yield to U-Turn”, as shown on the
  attached Exhibit A; and 2) Crenshaw Boulevard/Chadwick Lane - Install a right turn
  only lane for southbound Crenshaw Boulevard at Chadwick Lane with appropriate
  signing.

  Community Development/Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as
  per the agenda material).

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF was pleased with the sign shown in recommendation
  number one. She confirmed with Community Development/Public Works Director
  Wahba that cars would have enough time to merge in the outlined traffic plan for
  recommendation two.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired about the number of accidents listed in the
  staff report at the Crenshaw Blvd/Palos Verdes Dr. North intersection. Community
  Development/Public Works Director Wahba clarified that the number of listed
  accidents in the staff report were not specific to U-turn/right-turn incidents, but
  included all incidents that occurred in the general intersection.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE TWO TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ITEMS: 1)
  CRENSHAW BOULEVARD/PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH - INSTALL
  TWO SIGNS THAT STATE: “RIGHT HAND TURN ON RED MUST YIELD
  TO U-TURN”, AS SHOWN ON THE ATTACHED EXHIBIT A; AND 2)
  CRENSHAW BOULEVARD/CHADWICK LANE - INSTALL A RIGHT TURN
  ONLY LANE FOR SOUTHBOUND CRENSHAW BOULEVARD AT
  CHADWICK LANE WITH APPROPRIATE SIGNING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN announced his reelection to the Executive Committee
of the Clean Power Alliance (CPA). He also reported that CPA is facing some fiscal
challenges due to COVID-19 and some customers’ inability to pay bills.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 14, 2020
 COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported on yesterday’s South Bay Cities Council of
Governments’ (SBCCOG) Steering Committee meeting, including the growth of the South
Bay Fiber Network program.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF virtually attended the California Association of Councils of
Governments’ (CALCOG) Board of Directors meeting that was held this month.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF virtually attended the Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce’s
Legislative Affairs Committee meeting this morning. She inquired about local business
relief plans within Rolling Hills Estates after learning of relief measures being instituted in
Rancho Palos Verdes.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) did not meet in April, but will be meeting virtually on May 7, 2020.

MAYOR SCHMITZ announced that she and City Manager Grammer have been invited
by the Palos Verdes Chamber of Commerce to attend the Virtual Town Hall on Thursday
April 16, 2020 at 1:00pm. They will both sit on a panel with Mayor Cruikshank and City
Manager Mihranian from Rancho Palos Verdes.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR SCHMITZ commended City Manager Grammer and City Staff for being
innovative, proactive and committed to the City during this time.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF announced the Senior Resource Guide staff has created will
be available on the City’s website tomorrow.

City Manager Grammer thanked the Mayor and City Council for their leadership during
this crisis, and commended City Staff for their dedication and creativity, and for their
continued responsiveness to residents.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL echoed the Mayor’s sentiments, commending City Staff
for their hard work, the informative daily emails going out to the community and the
creative Virtual Recreation website.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN announced that Palos Verdes Transit’s Route 225 is
still in operation, and that the Dial-a-Ride program is also available for medical
appointments.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN echoed the Council’s gratitude for City staff, and also
commended the community for respecting the Social Distancing orders.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Davis stated that no reportable action was anticipated for either Closed
Session item this evening, but should any action be taken, it will be posted on the City
Clerk’s website immediately following the Closed Session.

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 14, 2020
 14.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR SCHMITZ announced that the City’s Earth Day Celebration scheduled for April
22, 2020 will be going virtual. Information will be on the City’s website and sent out to the
community through social media. The shredding event will be rescheduled for later in the
year.

At 8:14 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of those
who lost their lives due to COVID-19, including French Diplomat and Mayor of the City of
Antony, France, Patrick Devedjian, as well as all essential workers on the front lines of
the pandemic.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN said a few words in memory of his friend Patrick
Devedjian.

The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, April 28, 2020 at 7:00 p.m.
via teleconference.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit,  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 14, 2020
